sentences.ko: 걱정 마. 믿고 맡겨도 되는 사람이 봐 줄 거야.
sentences.text: I want you to know you're going to be in good hands.

alts.text: Don't worry, you're in good hands.
Please rest assured that you will be well taken care of.

sentences.note: **in good hands** 는 '믿을 만한 사람이 맡는다'는 뜻으로, 수술 전 환자를 안심시킬 때나 내 일을 다른 사람에게 넘기면서 걱정 말라고 할 때 씁니다. **I want you to know** 를 앞에 붙이면 진심을 꼭 전하고 싶다는 느낌이 납니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 어떻게 나올지 몰라서 그랬던 거잖아.
sentences.text: You didn't know how I was going to react.

alts.text: Didn't know how I'd take it, huh?
You were uncertain how I would respond.

sentences.note: 상대가 뭔가를 숨기거나 늦게 말했을 때 그 이유를 짚어 주는 말입니다. **how I was going to react** 대신 **how I'd take it** 이라고 해도 '내가 그걸 어떻게 받아들일지'라는 같은 뜻이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 젤을 설명서에 나온 것보다 좀 더 오래 발라 두긴 했어.
sentences.text: I I did leave the gel on a little longer than it said to.

alts.text: Okay, so I left the gel on kinda long.
I admit that I left the gel on somewhat longer than the instructions recommended.

sentences.note: **leave ~ on** 은 바르거나 붙인 것을 떼지 않고 그대로 두는 것으로, 팩이나 염색약, 마스크팩 얘기할 때 딱 맞습니다. **than it said to** 는 '설명서(포장)에 적힌 것보다'라는 뜻이고, 동사 앞의 **did** 는 '그건 인정해'라는 느낌을 줍니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 복도 맞은편 집 남자들이 우리한테 물풍선을 던지고 있어!
sentences.text: The guys across the hall are throwing water balloons at us.

alts.text: We're getting hit with water balloons by the guys across the hall!
Our neighbors across the hall are throwing water balloons at us.

sentences.note: **across the hall** 은 아파트나 기숙사에서 '복도 건너편 집'을 가리킬 때 씁니다. 앞집 이웃 얘기를 할 때 **the guys across the hall** 처럼 사람 뒤에 그대로 붙이면 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이게 왜 그렇게 이해가 안 돼?
sentences.text: Why is this so hard for you to get?

alts.text: Come on, what's so hard to get here?
I do not understand why this is so difficult for you to grasp.

sentences.note: 여기서 **get** 은 '이해하다'라는 뜻입니다. 여러 번 설명했는데도 상대가 못 알아들을 때 답답해서 하는 말이고, **so hard for you to get** 처럼 'for 사람 to 동사'로 누구한테 어려운지를 짚습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 뭐든 알려 주시면 정말 도움이 될 거예요.
sentences.text: Well, we appreciate anything you can tell us.

alts.text: Anything you've got helps, really.
We would be grateful for any information you are able to share.

sentences.note: **appreciate anything**는 '작은 거라도 좋으니 말해 달라'고 부드럽게 부탁할 때 씁니다. 상대가 망설일 때 부담을 덜어 주는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 지금은 좀 혼자 있고 싶어.
sentences.text: And I I just kind of want to be alone right now.

alts.text: Kinda need some space right now.
At the moment, I would simply prefer to be alone.

sentences.note: **kind of**를 끼우면 '좀' 정도로 말이 부드러워져서, 거절하거나 혼자 있고 싶다고 할 때 덜 차갑게 들립니다. **need some space**도 같은 자리에서 많이 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: We didn't know how you were going to react.

alts.text: Weren't sure how you'd take it.
We were uncertain how you would respond to the news.

sentences.note: 소식을 늦게 알렸거나 숨겼던 이유를 말할 때 **how you were going to react**를 씁니다. 더 편하게는 **how you'd take it**이라고 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 사실 지금쯤이면 벌써 와 있어야 하는데.
sentences.text: But actually, she should be here by now.

alts.text: Thought she'd be here already, though.
However, she ought to have arrived by this time.

sentences.note: **should be here by now**는 올 사람이 안 와서 슬슬 걱정될 때 하는 말입니다. 택배나 버스에도 그대로 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 와, 이제 내 의상이 제일 구린 건 아니네.
sentences.text: Wow, I don't have the worst costume anymore.

alts.text: Ha, mine's not the worst one now.
Well, my costume is no longer the worst one here.

sentences.note: 핼러윈 파티처럼 다들 차려입은 자리에서, 나보다 더한 사람이 나타나 안심될 때 씁니다. **anymore**를 끝에 붙이면 '이제는 아니다'라는 뜻이 돼요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends
